title: The POSTURE operand in ZPA policy rules
aliases: client connector posture profile condition set

prose.text: POSTURE criteria point a rule at a profile and at its verification result.

checks.do: Which value the lhs holds: the posture_udid, not the id and not the name.
Whether rhs true or false is meant: VERIFIED or VERIFICATION FAILED, and whether devices with no result are expected under false.
Whether the rule's client type is Client Connector, since posture criteria work only with it.
Whether the rule family accepts POSTURE: isolation rules do not.
Whether the rule is for the machine tunnel, where posture profile criteria need Zscaler Client Connector 3.9 or later.

lhs-is-udid.statement: A POSTURE operand's lhs is the profile's posture_udid, not its resource id: the data source note says to export posture_udid instead of the id, and the access rule documentation says lhs is the posture_udid.

quotes: the following parameter must be exported: ``posture_udid`` instead of the ``id`` of the resource.

rhs-verified.statement: In a POSTURE operand rhs true means VERIFIED and rhs false means VERIFICATION FAILED.

console-states.statement: In the console each posture profile in a condition set is set to VERIFIED, meaning Zscaler Client Connector verified the device against the profile's criteria, or VERIFICATION FAILED, meaning it was unable to verify the device against them.

quotes: VERIFIED: Zscaler Client Connector verified the user's device against the criteria specified in the posture profile.
VERIFICATION FAILED: Zscaler Client Connector was unable to verify the user's device against the criteria specified in the posture profile.

condition-sets.statement: A rule can have up to 10 Client Connector Posture Profile condition sets, and each set can hold several posture profiles.

quotes: You can add up to 10 Client Connector Posture Profile condition sets to the rule.
Each condition set can contain multiple posture profiles to enforce on a user’s device.

v2-no-lookup.conditions: ValidatePolicyRuleConditions is the v2 validator; the v1 resources call ValidateConditions, which does the lookup (same split as zpa.saml-attributes.policy-criteria:v1-validates-lookup).

families.statement: The provider's access, forwarding, timeout and inspection rule resources, in their v1 and v2 forms, list POSTURE among their operand object types.

isolation-excluded.statement: The provider's isolation rule resources, v1 and v2, do not list POSTURE among their operand object types.
isolation-excluded.conditions: Absence claim from a search: the string "POSTURE" does not occur in either isolation resource file.

false-meaning.title: Whether rhs false matches a device that has never reported a result for the profile
false-meaning.detail: The console describes VERIFICATION FAILED as Client Connector being 'unable to verify' the device, which could include a device that has no result, but no source separates 'evaluated and failed' from 'not evaluated'. Unverified legacy statement: "A device that has never reported a result for a given posture profile is distinct from a device that reported a failure. The behavior ... is not documented." Test with a device that has not evaluated the profile.
false-meaning.blocks: using rhs false to cover non-compliant and unknown devices together

quotes: VERIFICATION FAILED: Zscaler Client Connector was unable to verify the user's device against the criteria specified in the posture profile.

wrong-lhs-effect.title: What a v2 rule does when the POSTURE lhs is not a posture UDID
wrong-lhs-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Using the wrong identifier silently produces a policy condition that never matches", and "The ZPA API validates at rule creation". The v1 provider rejects an unknown lhs (claim v1-lookup) and the v2 provider checks only that it is non-empty (claim v2-no-lookup); whether ZPA accepts such a condition and what it then does is not shown. Create a v2 rule with the profile id as lhs in a scratch tenant and read it back.
wrong-lhs-effect.blocks: saying a wrong identifier fails silently

operand-name-rewrite-scope.title: Whether the API rewrites the name of POSTURE and TRUSTED_NETWORK operands
operand-name-rewrite-scope.detail: Unverified legacy statement (operator field observation from production Terraform use): the API rewrites a policy operand's name to the referenced object's display name for connector and segment references, but not for `postureUdid` or `networkId`, which are opaque identifiers and stay stable across plan and apply. The sources show the SDK clearing operand names before an update, not which operand types the API rewrites. Plan twice after an apply on a rule with a posture and a trusted network operand and compare the operands.
operand-name-rewrite-scope.blocks: telling whether posture and trusted-network operands cause drift in Terraform plans

posture-isolation.summary: Whether a posture profile can be referenced in an isolation policy.

quotes: This data source can then be referenced in an Access Policy, Timeout policy, Forwarding Policy, Inspection Policy or Isolation Policy.

positions.says: The data source can be referenced in an Isolation Policy.
The isolation rule resource's operand type list has no POSTURE.

posture-isolation.impact: A configuration that follows the data source documentation and puts a POSTURE operand in an isolation rule is rejected by the provider schema.
